note: Track beat (theory-basics), step 5: quarters, eighths and sixteenths mixed, a bar of each, then a change on every beat of one bar, then a new order over drums. Missing: a rhythm tool that shows a written bar and listens to the claps; backing-band's click sounds only the beat, so each bar is given as a count in the text.

exercise.title: Quarters, eighths and sixteenths in one bar
exercise.why: Quarters, eighths and sixteenths split the same beat into one, two and four, so as long as the numbers of your count stay on the click you can change from one to another on any beat.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome. Clap a bar of quarters, a bar of eighths and a bar of sixteenths, round and round, and count aloud: "1 2 3 4", then "1 and 2 and", then "1 e and a".
Listen for the numbers of your count: they land on the click in all three bars.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Clap one bar that goes quarter, two eighths, four sixteenths, quarter, and count it aloud: "1, 2 and, 3 e and a, 4".
When you can change from beat to beat without slowing down or rushing, try a faster stage. Use the Stage selector below to change the tempo, then press Play to start the metronome again.
If the sixteenths run past the next click, go back a stage and say the count for a bar before you clap it.

Press Play below to start the drums. Clap the bar the other way round: four sixteenths, two eighths, quarter, quarter, counting "1 e and a, 2 and, 3, 4".
Then make up a bar of your own from the three, and clap it until it comes round the same every time.
If you lose the beat, press Click below to switch the metronome on and clap quarters for a bar.
